objective: Prove: in a loop of r rule-60 rings with contacts reading their left neighbours (or both neighbours, under the no-overlap condition) on both rings, the feedback matrix is K = z(A + cA^-1) with A a weighted cyclic shift and c = a^(s-2); when the positions sum to rs/2, every diagonal entry of (I - K)^-1 is 1, so every contact binds both its rings at every lag at every ring size; and the feedback is a finite sum exactly when r is a power of two.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (by hand; finite claims checked): in a loop of r rule-60 rings the feedback is K = z(A + cA^-1) with A a weighted cyclic shift and c = a^(s-2); when the positions sum to rs/2 every diagonal entry of (I - K)^-1 is 1, so every contact binds both its rings at every lag at every ring size, for every r (the antipodal loops for every r and even s); the feedback is a finite sum exactly when r is a power of two and the loop is balanced.
title: Balance cancels the feedback in loops of any length
